citations: 29 CFR 1910.146(b), definitions of 'Hazardous atmosphere', 'Oxygen deficient atmosphere', 'Oxygen enriched atmosphere'
responses.text: 29 CFR (29 CFR 1910.146(b), definitions of 'Hazardous atmosphere', 'Oxygen deficient atmosphere', 'Oxygen enriched atmosphere', Permit-required confined spaces) states: Atmospheric oxygen concentration below 19.5 percent or above 23.5 percent See 29 CFR 1910.146(b), definitions of 'Hazardous atmosphere', 'Oxygen deficient atmosphere', 'Oxygen enriched atmosphere'.

29 CFR (29 CFR 1910.146(b), definition of 'Hazardous atmosphere', paragraph (1), Permit-required confined spaces) states: Flammable gas, vapor, or mist in excess of 10 percent of its lower flammable limit (LFL) See 29 CFR 1910.146(b), definition of 'Hazardous atmosphere', paragraph (1).

29 CFR (29 CFR 1910.333(a)(1), Selection and use of work practices) states: Live parts that operate at less than 50 volts to ground need not be deenergized if there will be no increased exposure to electrical burns or to explosion due to electric arcs. See 29 CFR 1910.333(a)(1).

29 CFR (29 CFR 1910.335(a)(1)(iv) and (a)(1)(v), Safeguards for personnel protection) states: Employees shall wear nonconductive head protection wherever there is a danger of head injury from electric shock or burns See 29 CFR 1910.335(a)(1)(iv) and (a)(1)(v).

29 CFR (29 CFR 1910.157(e)(2) and (e)(3), Portable fire extinguishers) states: The employer shall assure that portable fire extinguishers are subjected to an annual maintenance check. See 29 CFR 1910.157(e)(2) and (e)(3).

29 CFR (29 CFR 1910.157(d)(6), Portable fire extinguishers) states: The employer shall distribute portable fire extinguishers or other containers of Class D extinguishing agent for use by employees so that the travel distance from the combustible metal working area to any extinguishing agent is 75 feet (22.9 m) or less. See 29 CFR 1910.157(d)(6).

29 CFR (29 CFR 1910.106(a)(19)(iii) and (iv), Flammable liquids) states: Category 4 shall include liquids having flashpoints above 140 See 29 CFR 1910.106(a)(19)(iii) and (iv).

responses.text: 29 CFR (29 CFR 1910.1200(c), definitions of 'Hazard statement' and 'Precautionary statement', Hazard communication) states: Hazard statement means a statement assigned to a hazard class and category that describes the nature of the hazard See 29 CFR 1910.1200(c), definitions of 'Hazard statement' and 'Precautionary statement'.

29 CFR (29 CFR 1910.1200(c), definition of 'Signal word', Hazard communication) states: Signal word means a word used to indicate the relative level of severity of hazard See 29 CFR 1910.1200(c), definition of 'Signal word'.

29 CFR (29 CFR 1910.1200(g)(2), Hazard communication) states: includes at least the following section numbers and headings, and associated information under each heading, in the order listed See 29 CFR 1910.1200(g)(2).

29 CFR (29 CFR 1910.1200(c), definition of 'Pictogram', Hazard communication) states: Eight pictograms are designated under this standard for application to a hazard category. See 29 CFR 1910.1200(c), definition of 'Pictogram'.

29 CFR (29 CFR 1910.95(g)(5)(i) and (g)(5)(ii), Occupational noise exposure) states: Within 6 months of an employee's first exposure at or above the action level, the employer shall establish a valid baseline audiogram See 29 CFR 1910.95(g)(5)(i) and (g)(5)(ii).

29 CFR (29 CFR 1910.95(g)(10)(i), Occupational noise exposure) states: a standard threshold shift is a change in hearing threshold relative to the baseline audiogram of an average of 10 dB or more at 2000, 3000, and 4000 Hz in either ear See 29 CFR 1910.95(g)(10)(i).

29 CFR (29 CFR 1910.147(c)(7)(iii), The control of hazardous energy (lockout/tagout)) states: Retraining shall be provided for all authorized and affected employees whenever there is a change in their job assignments See 29 CFR 1910.147(c)(7)(iii).

29 CFR (29 CFR 1910.147(c)(6)(i)(D), The control of hazardous energy (lockout/tagout)) states: Where tagout is used for energy control, the periodic inspection shall include a review, between the inspector and each authorized and affected employee See 29 CFR 1910.147(c)(6)(i)(D).

29 CFR (29 CFR 1910.147(b), definition of 'Energy isolating device', The control of hazardous energy (lockout/tagout)) states: Push buttons, selector switches and other control circuit type devices are not energy isolating devices. See 29 CFR 1910.147(b), definition of 'Energy isolating device'.

29 CFR (29 CFR 1910.147(f)(3)(ii)(D), The control of hazardous energy (lockout/tagout)) states: Each authorized employee shall affix a personal lockout or tagout device to the group lockout device, group lockbox, or comparable mechanism when he or she begins work See 29 CFR 1910.147(f)(3)(ii)(D).

29 CFR (29 CFR 1910.147(f)(4), The control of hazardous energy (lockout/tagout)) states: Specific procedures shall be utilized during shift or personnel changes to ensure the continuity of lockout or tagout protection See 29 CFR 1910.147(f)(4).

29 CFR (29 CFR 1910.147(c)(1), The control of hazardous energy (lockout/tagout)) states: The employer shall establish a program consisting of energy control procedures, employee training and periodic inspections See 29 CFR 1910.147(c)(1).

29 CFR (29 CFR 1910.119(e)(6), Process safety management of highly hazardous chemicals) states: At least every five (5) years after the completion of the initial process hazard analysis, the process hazard analysis shall be updated and revalidated See 29 CFR 1910.119(e)(6).

29 CFR (29 CFR 1910.119(o)(1) and (o)(5), Process safety management of highly hazardous chemicals) states: Employers shall retain the two (2) most recent compliance audit reports. See 29 CFR 1910.119(o)(1) and (o)(5).

29 CFR (29 CFR 1910.119(g)(2), Process safety management of highly hazardous chemicals) states: Refresher training shall be provided at least every three years, and more often if necessary See 29 CFR 1910.119(g)(2).

29 CFR (29 CFR 1910.119(m)(1) and (m)(2), Process safety management of highly hazardous chemicals) states: An incident investigation shall be initiated as promptly as possible, but not later than 48 hours following the incident. See 29 CFR 1910.119(m)(1) and (m)(2).

29 CFR (29 CFR 1910.119(m)(7) and (o)(5), Process safety management of highly hazardous chemicals) states: Incident investigation reports shall be retained for five years. See 29 CFR 1910.119(m)(7) and (o)(5).
29 CFR (29 CFR 1910.119(a)(1)(ii), Process safety management of highly hazardous chemicals) states: in a quantity of 10,000 pounds See 29 CFR 1910.119(a)(1)(ii).

40 CFR (40 CFR 68.79(a), Compliance audits) states: at least every three years to verify that the procedures and practices developed under this subpart are adequate and are being followed See 40 CFR 68.79(a).
